subtitle: std::<system_error> — the C++11 diagnostic-code facility: the error_category abstract base, the error_code / error_condition value types, the system_error exception (deriving from runtime_error), the errc scoped enum, the is_error_code_enum / is_error_condition_enum customisation-point traits, the make_error_code / make_error_condition factories, and the generic_category / system_category singleton accessors. Like <typeinfo>, <new> and <stdexcept>, these are runtime-and-ABI-provided types: error_category is abstract with virtual members, the category singletons are compared by address, and errc maps to runtime-provided messages — so restd ships identity-preserving using-declaration re-exports (catch(std::system_error&) catches a restd-thrown one and vice versa; the one true category singletons are shared; relational/equality operators arrive via ADL on the std operand type, operator<=> from std on C++20+). Two genuine restd additions: the is_error_*_enum _v variables back-port from std's C++17 to C++14 (variable templates), and the hash<error_code> / hash<error_condition> specialisations — deferred out of <functional> to ship with their owning module — land here, with hash<error_condition> back-ported from std's C++17 to C++11 (a six-year lead). Everything is C++11 in std, so there are no back-ports of the core types; the whole module is gated at C++11 (no C++98 path). Depends on restd <functional> for the hash primary (shipped); no unmet restd dependencies.
legend_blurb: Per-symbol coverage of the C++11 <system_error> header. The error_category base, error_code / error_condition, system_error, errc, the is_error_*_enum traits, the make_error_* factories and the *_category accessors are all runtime-tied, so each is an identity-preserving re-export from std (like <typeinfo> / <stdexcept>). RESTD AHEAD OF STD: the _v trait variables back-port to C++14 and hash<error_condition> back-ports to C++11 (std: C++17). No C++98 path; 13/13 shipped at the C++11 floor.

symbols.name: error_category
symbols.notes: Identity-preserving using-declaration re-export of std::error_category, the abstract polymorphic base whose concrete instances (generic_category(), system_category(), user categories) are runtime-provided singletons compared by address. That identity cannot be reproduced portably, so restd re-exports rather than defines — restd::error_category IS std::error_category. Lives in system_error/error_category.hpp.
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98. <system_error> is a C++11 header: error_category is a runtime-provided abstract polymorphic facility whose category singletons are compared by address identity, and errc is a C++11 scoped enumeration — neither has a portable C++98 implementation. restd re-exports the std types (identity-preserving) on C++11+; the whole module is gated on D_ENV_LANG_IS_CPP11_OR_HIGHER and expands to nothing on C++98/03.

symbols.name: error_code
symbols.notes: Re-export of std::error_code (an integer value + a category reference). Its value depends on the runtime category singletons, so restd re-exports rather than reimplements; identity is preserved. The relational/equality operators are free functions in namespace std found by ADL on the (std) operand type, so they keep working under the restd spelling with no re-declaration; operator<=> arrives from std on C++20+. Lives in system_error/error_code.hpp.

symbols.name: system_error
symbols.notes: Re-export of std::system_error, the exception thrown for error_code-bearing failures; derives from std::runtime_error and carries an error_code. Identity preservation means catch(std::system_error&) catches a restd-thrown system_error and vice versa, and it stays catchable as restd::runtime_error / restd::exception. Lives in system_error/system_error.hpp.

symbols.name: errc
symbols.notes: Re-export of the std::errc scoped enumeration (enumerators mirror the POSIX errno constants). errc is the canonical error_CONDITION enum — is_error_condition_enum<errc> is true while is_error_code_enum<errc> is false. Meaningful only with the runtime category machinery, so restd re-exports rather than back-porting a struct-wrapper enum to C++98. Lives in system_error/errc.hpp.

symbols.name: is_error_code_enum

Lives in system_error/is_error_code_enum.hpp.

symbols.name: hash<error_code>
symbols.notes: restd::hash specialisation for error_code — deferred out of <functional> to ship with its owning module (this header), as documented in restd_modules.md §13.7. Specialises the empty restd::hash primary; combines value() with the address-identity of category() via reinterpret_cast, so it is not constexpr on any tier (matching std and restd's pointer-hash specialisation). Lives in system_error/hash.hpp.
